Hi Anna / Jenna,

Thanks for sending the redlined Order Form — appreciate the quick turnaround. I reviewed the high-level asks and pulled in Ben (sales ops) and Kimberly (legal) to confirm a few points so we can give you a consolidated response. Key things we want to confirm from your redlines:

- Minimum commit phasing: you’ve proposed a quarterly ramp (25%/25%/25%/25%) for the first year. Is that required for billing purposes, or is Leafstream open to monthly invoicing with a quarterly true-up?
- Net terms: the redline shows Net 45. Our standard at this stage is Net 30 for self-serve/SMB tiers and Net 45 for reserved capacity with approved finance. Can you confirm whether Net 45 is a hard requirement from procurement?
- Invoice entity & tax residency: your team requested VAT/residency clause edits and an indemnity for withholding tax. Please confirm the billing entity for Leafstream (US entity vs EU) and whether you require us to provide W9 / VAT registration evidence.
- Invoicing cadence & sample: I attached a sample invoice schema to show how fees, credits, and minimum commit true-ups would appear. Does that match your AP requirements?

If you can confirm those four items, we’ll prepare a clean order form and a marked-up MSA cross-reference for Kimberly’s review.

Best,
Sergio
Sergio Alvarez | Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference

On Thu, Sep 3, 2026 at 13:40 PM Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com> wrote:
> Sergio / Anna / team — looping in a couple ops notes from my side:
>
> 1) Billing cadence: We can support monthly invoices per entity and run a quarterly true-up to meet Leafstream’s CapEx needs. That would appear on the invoice as both the month invoices and a quarterly 'commit true-up' line item. See attached sample.
> 2) Minimum commit: We can structure the Order Form with a staged minimum commit schedule (Q1: 25%, Q2: 25%, etc.). For accounting clarity we’ll include a callout that unused commit in a quarter rolls into a single trailing true-up within the year (not refundable).
> 3) Net terms: Finance notes that Net 45 is acceptable for corporate-level procurements with a PO and customer credit profile; if procurement needs Net 30 we can propose Net 30 with a 2% early pay discount or connect for a credit review.
> 4) Tax withholdings / VAT: We require entity-level billing in cases where reverse charge applies. For the W9 / VAT evidence ask: we can provide a W9 and US tax residency confirmation; for EU VAT we'd need the EU entity VAT registration — please confirm target billing entity.
>
> Next steps: if Anna confirms Leafstream Health Inc (US) as billing entity and accepts quarterly ramp + Net 45, I’ll prepare the invoice schedule and PO fields for your procurement team to sign off.

> Team / Anna — a few legal points from our end after scanning the redline:

> - Tax indemnity: We can accept reverse charge language for EU subsidiaries but cannot accept broad indemnities for withholding taxes across unrelated third-party jurisdictions. We’ll propose a narrowly tailored clause limited to the billing entity’s statutory obligations.
